brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three bases at level 0 (piece:0,0,0, piece:0,1,0, piece:1,0,0) and three bases at level 1 stacked with snaps (piece:0,0,1, piece:0,1,1, piece:1,0,1) – 6 bases forming two full storeys.
Two full bins on upper storey (bin:0,0,1 and bin:0,1,1) dressed with workshop props (heap-screws-bin, heap-nuts-bin) plus two drawer frames provide bench-top small-parts storage.
Two notch drawer frames installed: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 at q-1,r1 level0 and notch:0#1,-1#notch4 at q1,r-1 level0, both hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf.

finish.summary: Built a compact two-storey tower (3-cell footprint × 2 levels, ~6 bases) with two notch drawer frames on the ground floor flanking the tower and two open bins on the upper floor for workbench small-parts storage. House rules capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied, mesh clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
